All off-line transactions done through BCs must be accounted for and reflected in the bank's books by the end of the day. II. The BC issues a receipt on behalf of the bank as acknowledgment for cash collected from a customer. III. The bank must carry out a detailed review of the performance of its BCs at least once a quarter. Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.concept: Operational safeguards for BCs
solution.explanation: The Directions require the bank's arrangements to provide that off-line transactions reflect in the bank's books by the end of the day (I right) and that a receipt is issued on behalf of the bank for cash collected (II right). The detailed review of BC performance is required at least once in a year, not every quarter (III wrong).
steps: II: receipt on bank's behalf → true
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option including III is wrong, because the minimum frequency for the detailed review is once a year.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Issuing a receipt on behalf of the bank as acknowledgment for cash collected from the customer; All off-line transactions are accounted for and reflect in the books of the bank by the end of the day
A bank shall carry out a detailed review of the performance of various BCs engaged by it at least once in a year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's revised circular on the Lead Bank Scheme issued on 19 June 2026, in which districts must Special Sub-Committees (SSCs) of the District Consultative Committee be set up, and with whom as Convenor?

options.text: Districts with a CD ratio below 40% and Annual Credit Plan achievement below 100% in the preceding year; the Lead District Manager
Districts with a CD ratio below 40% or no banking outlet in some villages; the RBI Lead District Officer
Districts with a CD ratio below 60% in the preceding year; the District Collector
Districts with Annual Credit Plan achievement below 75%; the SLBC Convenor Bank

solution.concept: Lead Bank Scheme, 2026 circular
solution.explanation: The revised Lead Bank Scheme circular (19 June 2026) provides that in districts with a CD ratio of less than 40% as well as ACP achievement of less than 100% for the preceding financial year, Special Sub-Committees of the DCC, with the LDM as Convenor, shall be set up to monitor the CD ratio. Both conditions must hold.
steps: Trigger: CD ratio < 40% AND ACP achievement < 100% (preceding FY)
SSC of the DCC, LDM as Convenor
solution.why_others_wrong: The threshold is 40% (not 60%) and needs both conditions, not either; the Convenor is the LDM, not the Collector, the RBI LDO or the SLBC Convenor Bank.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Districts with a CD ratio below 40% and Annual Credit Plan achievement below 100% in the preceding year; the Lead District Manager

fact_checks.claim: In districts having CD Ratio less than 40 percent as well as ACP achievement less than 100% for the preceding financial year, Special Sub-Committees (SSCs) of the DCC, with LDM as Convenor shall be set up to monitor the CD Ratio.
The revised Circular on the Lead Bank Scheme (LBS) has been issued today.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Financial Benchmarks India Pvt. Ltd (FBIL), the independent administrator of rupee interest rate and foreign exchange benchmarks recognised by RBI, was jointly floated by:

options.text: CCIL, NSDL and the State Bank of India
FIMMDA, FEDAI and the Indian Banks' Association

solution.concept: Benchmark administration in Indian financial markets
solution.explanation: On RBI's acceptance of a committee's recommendations, FBIL was set up as an independent company jointly floated by the Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association (FIMMDA), the Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India (FEDAI) and the IBA. Its first benchmark, from 22 July 2015, was the 'FBIL-Overnight MIBOR', which replaced the FIMMDA-NSE overnight rate.
steps: Industry bodies of the money/debt market (FIMMDA), forex market (FEDAI) and banks (IBA) -> FBIL
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI and SEBI are regulators, not FBIL's promoters; CCIL is a clearing house (FBIL's calculation agent for some benchmarks), not an owner; NABARD, SIDBI and EXIM Bank are development finance institutions.
solution.final_answer: Option C: FIMMDA, FEDAI and the Indian Banks' Association

fact_checks.claim: FBIL, an independent company jointly floated by the FIMMDA, the FEDAI and the IBA ... The FBIL will act as an independent benchmark administrator.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Unique Identifiers in Financial Markets Directions, 2026, the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) that parties to a financial transaction must hold is a unique identity code of how many characters?

solution.concept: Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)
solution.explanation: The LEI is a 20-character code that identifies the parties to a financial transaction worldwide. Under RBI's directions, non-individual entities need an LEI to undertake OTC transactions in government securities, money market, foreign exchange and derivatives markets.
solution.why_others_wrong: 12 characters is the length of an ISIN; 16 is the length of a typical card number; 52 is the maximum length of the Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) for OTC derivatives under the same directions.

fact_checks.claim: LEI code, a 20-character unique identity code assigned to entities who are parties to a financial transaction

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Unique Identifiers in Financial Markets Directions of March 2026 introduce a Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) from 1 January 2027. Which description of the UTI is correct?

options.text: It identifies each OTC derivative transaction, has a maximum of 52 characters and begins with the LEI of the generating entity
It identifies each UPI payment, has 12 digits and begins with the payer's bank IFSC
It identifies each investor in mutual funds, has 10 characters and is the same as the PAN
It identifies each government security, has 20 characters and is issued by CCIL

solution.concept: Identifiers in OTC markets: LEI and UTI
solution.explanation: Section B of the 2026 directions, effective 1 January 2027, requires a Unique Transaction Identifier for OTC derivative transactions. It can be up to 52 characters long and is formed from the LEI of the entity generating it followed by a unique identifier, so that each trade can be traced in trade repositories.
steps: UTI = transaction-level identifier for OTC derivatives
Structure: LEI of generating entity + unique code
solution.why_others_wrong: UPI transaction references, PAN-based investor identity and ISINs of securities are other identifiers; none is the UTI defined by these directions.
solution.final_answer: Option A: It identifies each OTC derivative transaction, has a maximum of 52 characters and begins with the LEI of the generating entity

fact_checks.claim: It shall have a maximum of 52 characters comprising the LEI of the generating entity followed by a unique identifier
Section B (UTI) shall come into effect from January 01, 2027.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI issued new Credit Derivatives Directions in June 2026, replacing the 2022 directions. What did they mainly introduce?

options.text: Credit default swaps on government securities and State Development Loans
Derivatives on credit indices and total return swaps on corporate bonds
Permission for market-makers to sell credit default swaps to individuals
Credit derivatives on asset-backed and mortgage-backed securities

solution.concept: Credit derivatives market in India
solution.explanation: The Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026 (in force from 25 June 2026) allow market-makers and users to deal in CDS and total return swaps (TRS); their stated purpose is the introduction of derivatives on credit indices and TRS on corporate bonds. Reference obligations are money market debt instruments and rated (and certain unrated infrastructure SPV) INR corporate bonds.
steps: New: credit-index derivatives and TRS on corporate bonds
solution.why_others_wrong: G-secs and SDLs are not eligible reference obligations; market-makers may not offer CDS to individuals; ABS/MBS are expressly excluded.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Derivatives on credit indices and total return swaps on corporate bonds

fact_checks.claim: Please refer to Paragraph 13 of the Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies regarding the introduction of derivatives on credit indices and total return swaps on corporate bonds.
These Directions shall come into force on June 25, 2026. Market-makers and users may undertake transactions in CDS and TRS contracts.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Government Securities Lending (GSL) Directions, 2023, which statement about Treasury Bills is correct?

options.text: T-bills are the only securities that can be lent under GSL
T-bills cannot be lent under GSL, but may be placed as collateral in a GSL transaction
T-bills can be lent under GSL, but cannot be placed as collateral
T-bills can neither be lent nor placed as collateral under GSL

solution.concept: Securities lending in the G-sec market
solution.explanation: In a GSL transaction the owner lends eligible government securities to a borrower for a fee against other government securities as collateral. Central Government securities excluding T-bills are eligible for lending, whereas the collateral may be Central Government securities including T-bills, or State Government securities. The minimum tenor is one day.
steps: Collateral: Central G-secs including T-bills, and SGSs
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong option reverses or misstates the two rules: T-bills are excluded from lending but allowed as collateral.
solution.final_answer: Option B: T-bills cannot be lent under GSL, but may be placed as collateral in a GSL transaction

fact_checks.claim: Government securities issued by the Central Government excluding Treasury Bills shall be eligible for lending under a GSL transaction.
Central Government securities (including Treasury Bills) and State Government securities can be placed as collateral. The minimum tenor of a GSL transaction shall be one day.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Electronic Trading Platforms (ETP) Directions, 2025, which of the following is an eligibility requirement for an entity seeking authorisation to operate an ETP?

options.text: A company incorporated in India with a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore, maintained at all times
A scheduled commercial bank with a minimum net worth of ₹500 crore
Any foreign entity registered with IOSCO, with no net worth requirement
A recognised stock exchange with a minimum net worth of ₹100 crore

solution.concept: Regulation of electronic trading platforms by RBI
solution.explanation: An ETP is any electronic system, other than a recognised stock exchange, on which securities, money market instruments, forex instruments or derivatives are traded. To operate one, an entity must be a company incorporated in India, keep a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore at all times, and it (or at least two key managerial persons) must have at least three years' experience of operating trading infrastructure in financial markets.
steps: Net worth: ₹5 crore, at all times
solution.why_others_wrong: Recognised stock exchanges are outside the ETP definition; banks' own systems are a separate exemption and no ₹500 crore rule exists; foreign entities without incorporation in India are not eligible.
solution.final_answer: Option A: A company incorporated in India with a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore, maintained at all times

fact_checks.claim: ETP means any electronic system, other than a recognised stock exchange, on which transactions in eligible instruments are contracted.
The entity shall be a company incorporated in India ... minimum net-worth of ₹5 crore (Rupees five crore only) ... maintained at all times.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026, which of the following entities is NOT eligible to act as a market-maker in credit derivatives?

options.text: NaBFID (National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development)
An NBFC in the Middle Layer

solution.concept: Market-makers in credit derivatives
solution.explanation: Eligible market-makers are scheduled commercial banks other than small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks and RRBs; standalone primary dealers; NBFCs in the Upper and Middle Layers (including HFCs); and EXIM Bank, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI and NaBFID. A small finance bank is expressly excluded.
steps: SCBs eligible except SFBs, PBs, LABs, RRBs
SPDs, NBFC-UL/ML and the AIFIs including NaBFID eligible
Hence the SFB is not eligible
solution.why_others_wrong: Middle Layer NBFCs, standalone PDs and NaBFID are all listed as eligible market-makers.
solution.final_answer: Option D: A small finance bank

fact_checks.claim: The following entities shall be eligible to act as market-makers in credit derivatives: (a) Scheduled Commercial Banks, except Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, Local Area Banks and Regional Rural Banks; ... (c) NBFCs – Upper Layer and NBFCs – Middle Layer (including Housing Financial Companies)
Market-makers include standalone primary dealers ... and EXIM, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI and NaBFID.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A resident company with a net worth of ₹400 crore and turnover of ₹900 crore (latest audited) holds ₹40 crore face value of a rated corporate bond. It approaches a bank to buy CDS protection of ₹50 crore on that bond. Under RBI's Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026, what is the position?

options.text: It is a retail user; it may buy protection only to hedge, for a notional of at most ₹40 crore
It is a retail user; it may buy the full ₹50 crore as long as it holds the bond
It is a non-retail user; it may buy the full ₹50 crore of protection for any purpose
It is a retail user and is not allowed to buy CDS protection at all

solution.concept: Retail and non-retail users of credit derivatives
solution.explanation: A resident company is non-retail only if its net worth is at least ₹500 crore or its turnover at least ₹1,000 crore; this company meets neither, so it is a retail user. A non-individual retail user may buy protection only for hedging; it must have exposure to the reference asset, and the notional cannot exceed the face value of the reference obligation held, i.e. ₹40 crore.
steps: ₹400 cr < ₹500 cr and ₹900 cr < ₹1,000 cr -> retail
Notional cap = face value held = ₹40 crore
solution.why_others_wrong: It fails both non-retail thresholds; even a hedger cannot buy notional above the face value it holds; retail users other than individuals are allowed to buy protection for hedging.
solution.final_answer: Option A: It is a retail user; it may buy protection only to hedge, for a notional of at most ₹40 crore

fact_checks.claim: Resident companies with (a) minimum net worth of ₹500 crore; or (b) minimum turnover of ₹1,000 crore, as per the latest audited financial statements ... Any user who is not eligible to be classified as a non-retail user shall be classified as a retail user.

A resident retail user, other than an individual, shall be allowed to buy protection only for the purpose of hedging ... shall not buy a credit derivative contract(s) with notional amount higher than the face value of the reference obligation

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Consider the following statements based on RBI's market directions: I. Under the Financial Benchmark Administrators Directions, 2023, an administrator of a 'significant benchmark' must maintain a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore, against ₹1 crore for other benchmarks. II. Under the Unique Identifiers Directions, 2026, the LEI requirement for non-derivative foreign exchange transactions applies only to transactions of USD one million or more. III. Under the Financial Benchmark Administrators Directions, 2023, the methodology of a non-significant benchmark need be reviewed only once every three years. Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.concept: Benchmark administrators and LEI thresholds
solution.explanation: FBAs must be companies incorporated in India with net worth of ₹5 crore (significant benchmark) or ₹1 crore (non-significant), maintained at all times. For non-derivative forex, the LEI applies to transactions of USD 1 million or more. Statement III is wrong: a non-significant benchmark's methodology must be reviewed at least once a year.
steps: III: review at least once a year, not three years -> wrong
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option including III is wrong; 'I only' omits the correct statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Minimum net-worth of ₹5 crore for an FBA administering a significant benchmark and ₹1 crore for a non-significant benchmark ... at all times. The methodology [of a non-significant benchmark] shall be reviewed at least once in a year.
the LEI code shall be applicable only for transactions involving an amount equivalent to or exceeding USD one million

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Certificate of Deposit Directions, 2021, can a bank grant a loan against the security of a Certificate of Deposit (CD)?

options.text: Yes, but only against CDs issued by itself
No, unless specifically permitted by the Reserve Bank
Yes, freely, as CDs are negotiable instruments
Yes, up to 75% of the face value of the CD

solution.concept: Certificates of Deposit
solution.explanation: A CD is a negotiable money market instrument issued in demat form against funds deposited with a bank. Unlike ordinary term deposits, banks are not allowed to grant loans against CDs unless RBI specifically permits it; an issuer may, however, buy back its CDs before maturity, but only after seven days from issue.
steps: Loans against CDs: not allowed, save with RBI's specific permission
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no 75% margin rule for CDs; loans against own CDs are equally barred; negotiability allows transfer, not loans against CDs.
solution.final_answer: Option B: No, unless specifically permitted by the Reserve Bank

fact_checks.claim: Banks are not allowed to grant loans against CDs, unless specifically permitted by the Reserve Bank

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: RBI's 2024 directions on Commercial Paper also cover Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs) of original maturity up to one year. How are such NCDs described, and what tenor is permitted?

options.text: An unsecured instrument, with a tenor of one year to three years
A secured instrument, with a tenor of 90 days to one year
A secured instrument, with a tenor of 7 days to 90 days
An unsecured instrument, with a tenor of 7 days to one year

solution.concept: Short-term NCDs vs Commercial Paper
solution.explanation: Under the 2024 directions an NCD is a secured money market instrument with original or initial maturity up to one year, issued for 90 days to one year. CP, in contrast, is an unsecured promissory note issued for 7 days to one year. Both are issued in demat form in minimum denominations of ₹5 lakh.
steps: Tenor: 90 days to 1 year (CP: 7 days to 1 year)
solution.why_others_wrong: 7 days to one year is the CP tenor and CP is unsecured; 7-90 days and 1-3 years are not the NCD range.
solution.final_answer: Option B: A secured instrument, with a tenor of 90 days to one year

fact_checks.claim: NCD means a secured money market instrument with an original or initial maturity upto one year.
CPs run from 7 days to 1 year; NCDs run from 90 days to 1 year.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: Which of the following is permitted under RBI's Commercial Paper and short-term NCD Directions, 2024?

options.text: Issuing CP with a credit rating of A3 or above
Issuing CP with a call option exercisable after 30 days
Issuing CP in physical form to retail investors
Underwriting of a CP issue by a bank

solution.concept: Features of Commercial Paper
solution.explanation: CP must carry a minimum credit rating of A3 (SEBI's symbol and definition) and must be issued in dematerialised form. Issuing CP or NCDs with call/put options is not permitted, nor are underwriting and co-acceptance.
steps: Options, underwriting, physical form -> not permitted
solution.why_others_wrong: Call/put options are prohibited; underwriting and co-acceptance are prohibited; CPs must be issued in demat form only.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Issuing CP with a credit rating of A3 or above

fact_checks.claim: The minimum credit rating of the CP shall be A3 as per rating symbol and definition prescribed by SEBI. Issuance of a CP/NCD with options (call/put) is not permitted.
CPs and NCDs shall be issued in dematerialised form and held with a depository registered with SEBI. Underwriting and co-acceptance are not permitted.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: A company issued a 91-day Commercial Paper on 1 September 2026. Its cash position improves and it wants to buy back the CP from investors on 5 September 2026. Under RBI's CP Directions, 2024, which statement is correct?

options.text: It cannot buy back the CP at all before maturity
It can buy back on 5 September from any investors it chooses, at par value
It can buy back on 5 September only with SEBI's prior approval, and may resell the CP later

It cannot buy back on 5 September, as a CP may be bought back only after 7 days from issue; any later buyback must be offered to all investors on identical terms at the prevailing market price, and the CP extinguished

solution.concept: Buyback of Commercial Paper
solution.explanation: An issuer may buy back CP before maturity only after seven days from issue (NCDs only after 90 days). The offer must be made to all investors in that issue on identical terms, at the prevailing market price, and the bought-back CP is extinguished on the buyback date. 5 September is only four days after issue, so the buyback is not allowed then.
steps: Issue 1 Sep -> 5 Sep is 4 days later (< 7 days)
Later buyback: all investors, identical terms, market price, extinguished
solution.why_others_wrong: Selective buyback at par is not allowed; buyback is permitted after 7 days, not barred entirely; SEBI approval and resale of bought-back CP have no basis, as the CP must be extinguished.
solution.final_answer: Option D: It cannot buy back on 5 September, as a CP may be bought back only after 7 days from issue; any later buyback must be offered to all investors on identical terms at the prevailing market price, and the CP extinguished

fact_checks.claim: CPs can be bought back only after 7 days from issue, and NCDs only after 90 days. The offer must go to all investors on identical terms, at the prevailing market price. Bought-back instruments are extinguished on the buyback date.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: A bank issues a 182-day Certificate of Deposit of face value ₹25 crore at a discount, priced to give a yield of 7.30% (Actual/365). What is the issue price per ₹100 of face value, and into how many units of the minimum denomination allowed by RBI's CD Directions can the issue be divided?

solution.concept: Pricing of discounted money market instruments
solution.explanation: Price = 100 / (1 + yield × days/365) = 100 / (1 + 0.073 × 182/365) ≈ ₹96.49. CDs are issued in a minimum denomination of ₹5 lakh and multiples thereof, so ₹25 crore = 500 units of ₹5 lakh.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹96.36 treats 7.30% as a discount rate on face value, not a yield; 2,500 units assumes a ₹1 lakh denomination; ₹93.20 discounts for a full year instead of 182 days.

fact_checks.claim: CDs shall be issued in minimum denomination of ₹5 lakh and in multiples of ₹5 lakh thereafter.
CDs may be issued at a discount to face value or on a fixed or floating rate basis; banks may issue CDs for a minimum of seven days and up to one year.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to NSE Indices' factsheet of 30 October 2026, which sector has the highest weight in the Nifty 50?

solution.concept: Sectoral composition of the Nifty 50
solution.explanation: Financial Services made up 37.13% of the Nifty 50, far ahead of Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels (9.00%) and Information Technology (8.80%). The two largest constituents were HDFC Bank (9.95%) and ICICI Bank (9.39%).
steps: Financial Services 37.13% > Oil & Gas 9.00% > IT 8.80% > ... FMCG 5.36%
solution.why_others_wrong: Oil & Gas, IT and FMCG each have under 10% weight.

fact_checks.claim: Sector Weight(%): Financial Services 37.13; Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels 9.00; Information Technology 8.80; Fast Moving Consumer Goods 5.36

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 24 September 2026, SEBI's Board approved an enabling provision for issuing Depository Receipts (DRs) on units of REITs and InvITs. Where does the framework envisage such DRs being issued and listed to begin with?

options.text: On the SME platforms of NSE and BSE
Only on stock exchanges in the United States
In the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) in India

solution.concept: Foreign capital for REITs and InvITs
solution.explanation: To attract foreign capital to REITs and InvITs, SEBI approved amendments enabling DRs on their units. The framework envisages issue and listing of these DRs in the IFSC in India (GIFT City) to begin with, and all foreign investors, including NRIs, can invest in them.
steps: DRs on REIT/InvIT units -> IFSC in India first
solution.why_others_wrong: DRs are aimed at foreign investors, so domestic SME platforms and the Social Stock Exchange do not fit; the framework starts in India's IFSC, not on US exchanges.
solution.final_answer: Option C: In the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) in India

fact_checks.claim: The framework envisages issuance and listing of DRs on units of REITs and InvITs in the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) in India to begin with. Further, all foreign investors (including NRIs) can invest in such DRs.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the eligibility criteria in NSE Indices' Nifty 50 factsheet (October 2026), which require F&O eligibility, a minimum listing history and an impact-cost test, which of these companies can be considered for inclusion?

options.text: Q: in the F&O segment, listed 3 weeks, average impact cost 0.30% for 95% of observations (basket ₹10 crore)
P: in the F&O segment, listed 2 months, average impact cost 0.40% for 92% of observations (basket ₹10 crore)
S: in the F&O segment, listed 4 years, average impact cost 0.70% for 90% of observations (basket ₹10 crore)
R: not in the F&O segment, listed 5 years, average impact cost 0.20% for 99% of observations (basket ₹10 crore)

solution.concept: Liquidity and eligibility screens for the Nifty 50
solution.explanation: To qualify, a stock must have traded at an average impact cost of 0.50% or less for 90% of observations over six months for a basket of ₹100 million (₹10 crore), be allowed in the F&O segment, and have a listing history of at least one month at the cut-off date. Only P meets all three.
solution.why_others_wrong: Q fails the one-month listing rule, R fails the F&O rule, and S fails the impact-cost rule.
solution.final_answer: Option B: P: in the F&O segment, listed 2 months, average impact cost 0.40% for 92% of observations (basket ₹10 crore)

fact_checks.claim: For a stock to qualify for possible inclusion into the Nifty50, have traded at an average impact cost of 0.50% or less during the last six months for 90% of the observations, for the basket size of Rs. 100 Million.
Companies that are allowed to trade in F&O segment are only eligible to be constituent of the index. The Company should have a minimum listing history of 1 month as on the cutoff date.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 23 March 2026, SEBI's Board approved recommendations of the High-Level Committee on conflict of interest of its own Members and officials. Which of the following was among them?

options.text: The Chairman and Whole-Time Members must liquidate only their unlisted investments before joining
SEBI officials are barred from investing in mutual funds and all other pooled vehicles

The Chairman and Whole-Time Members are to be brought within the definition of 'insider', and new investments by officials in products of a single intermediary may not exceed 25% of their financial portfolio
Part-time Members of the Board must publicly disclose all their assets and liabilities every year

solution.concept: Conflict-of-interest framework within SEBI
solution.explanation: The Board approved bringing the Chairman and WTMs within the definition of 'insider', applying employees' trading restrictions to them, and a 25% cap on new investments by employees/WTMs/Chairman in products managed by a single SEBI-registered intermediary (with recusal if breached). Investments in regulated pooled vehicles remain allowed, and no public disclosure is required for Part-Time Members.
solution.why_others_wrong: No public disclosure is required of Part-Time Members; investments in mutual funds and professionally managed pooled vehicles are permitted; listed and unlisted equity holdings at joining must be liquidated, frozen or sold under the chosen option, not only unlisted ones.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The Chairman and Whole-Time Members are to be brought within the definition of 'insider', and new investments by officials in products of a single intermediary may not exceed 25% of their financial portfolio

fact_checks.claim: Chairman and WTMs to be brought within the definition of "insider".
New investments by employees / WTMs / Chairman in products managed by a single SEBI-registered intermediary may not exceed 25% of their financial portfolio.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In September 2026 SEBI's Board amended Regulation 62A of the LODR Regulations for issuers listing non-convertible debentures (NCDs) for the first time. What changed?

options.text: NCDs may no longer be issued on a private placement basis by listed entities
Such an issuer must now list all its outstanding unlisted NCDs within one month instead of three
All unlisted NCDs issued since 2015 must now be listed within three months
Such an issuer need no longer list all its outstanding unlisted NCDs; only prospective NCD issuances must be listed

solution.concept: Listing of debt securities
solution.explanation: Earlier, an entity proposing to list an NCD had to list all its outstanding unlisted NCDs issued on or after 1 January 2024 within three months of the new listing. SEBI removed this to ease costs (ISIN limits, covenant monitoring): the entity now has to list only prospective issuances, which should encourage new issuers to list debt.
steps: Old: list all outstanding unlisted NCDs (issued on/after 1 Jan 2024) within 3 months
New: only prospective issuances need listing
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options tighten rather than relax the rule, or describe changes that were not made.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Such an issuer need no longer list all its outstanding unlisted NCDs; only prospective NCD issuances must be listed

fact_checks.claim: to do away with the requirement for mandatory listing of all outstanding unlisted non-convertible debt securities ("NCD") by an issuer who proposes to list its NCD for the first time.
The amendment provides that an entity shall be required to list only prospective issuances of non-convertible debt securities.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: SEBI's Board on 24 September 2026 allowed FPIs to participate in non-cash settled, non-agricultural commodity derivatives contracts. What safeguard applies?

options.text: FPIs must take delivery of the commodity on expiry of every contract
FPIs must hold at least 50% of their positions until expiry
FPIs can trade only through the IFSC exchanges and must settle in US dollars
FPIs must exit their positions before the Tender Period (three days before expiry) and cannot increase positions from T-3

solution.concept: FPIs in exchange-traded commodity derivatives
solution.explanation: FPIs may now trade non-agricultural index derivatives and non-cash-settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, but must exit before a delivery obligation can arise, i.e. before the Tender Period that starts three days before expiry; they cannot increase positions from T-3. Residual open positions are devolved on the trading member/clearing member under a prior agreement.
steps: No increase in positions from T-3
solution.why_others_wrong: The whole point is to avoid delivery by FPIs; trading is on Indian commodity exchanges, not only IFSC; there is no minimum holding rule.
solution.final_answer: Option D: FPIs must exit their positions before the Tender Period (three days before expiry) and cannot increase positions from T-3

fact_checks.claim: a safeguard mechanism is proposed to ensure that FPIs exit their positions before entering the Tender Period, i.e. three (3) days before the expiry of the contract ... FPIs shall not be permitted to increase their positions from T-3 day.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under SEBI's Settlement Scheme, 2026 for non-genuine trades in illiquid stock options on BSE, the settlement amount is ₹1,44,000 for 1-5 contracts, ₹2,88,000 for 6-50 contracts, and, for 51 contracts and above, ₹7,20,000 plus ₹14,400 multiplied by the total number of contracts traded (not just those above 50). Entities P, Q and R traded 4, 50 and 75 contracts respectively. What is the total settlement amount payable by the three?

solution.concept: Settlement schemes under the SEBI Act
solution.explanation: P (4 contracts) pays ₹1,44,000; Q (50 contracts, still within 6-50) pays ₹2,88,000; R (75 contracts) pays ₹7,20,000 + 75 × ₹14,400 = ₹18,00,000. Total = ₹22,32,000. This fourth scheme, under Section 15JB of the SEBI Act, follows schemes of 2020, 2022 and 2024 for trades on BSE between 1 April 2014 and 30 September 2015.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹15,12,000 charges R only for the 25 contracts above 50; ₹33,84,000 wrongly puts Q (50 contracts) in the top slab (₹14,40,000); ₹23,76,000 wrongly puts P (4 contracts) in the 6-50 slab.

fact_checks.claim: Settlement Amount: 01-05 contracts ₹1,44,000; 06-50 ₹2,88,000; 51 and above ₹7,20,000 + ₹14,400 per contract. E.g. for 51 contracts, the SA would be ₹14,54,400

SEBI has decided to introduce a fourth (4th) Settlement Scheme ... under Section 15JB of the SEBI Act, 1992 ... for dealing with the matter of trading activities of certain entities in ISOs on Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under SEBI's circular of 26 February 2026 on categorisation of mutual fund schemes, which scheme category was discontinued, with existing schemes stopping all subscriptions immediately?

solution.concept: Categorisation and rationalisation of mutual fund schemes
solution.explanation: The 2026 circular re-grouped schemes into Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Life Cycle Funds and Other schemes (FoFs and passive schemes). The Solution Oriented category (retirement and children's funds) was discontinued; existing schemes had to stop subscriptions at once and be merged with similar schemes with SEBI's approval.
steps: Feb 2026 circular -> Solution Oriented category discontinued
New group added: Life Cycle Funds
solution.why_others_wrong: Arbitrage and Equity Savings remain hybrid categories, and FoFs remain under 'Other Schemes'.

fact_checks.claim: Solutions oriented scheme category is being discontinued w.e.f the date of the circular. Existing schemes in this category shall stop all subscriptions with immediate effect.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under SEBI's revised scheme categories of February 2026, what are the investment requirements of a Multi Cap Fund?

options.text: At least 75% in equity, with at least 25% each in large cap, mid cap and small cap companies
At least 65% in equity across market caps, with no minimum for any one segment
At least 80% in equity, of which at least 35% each in large cap and mid cap companies
At least 65% in equity, with at least 25% each in large cap and mid cap companies only

solution.concept: Equity scheme categories
solution.explanation: A Multi Cap Fund must invest at least 75% of total assets in equity, with minimums of 25% each in large, mid and small cap companies. The 65% equity floor with no segment minimum describes a Flexi Cap Fund, and 35% each in large and mid caps is the Large & Mid Cap Fund.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option 2 is Flexi Cap; option 3 mixes in the Large & Mid Cap rule; option 4 drops the small cap minimum.
solution.final_answer: Option A: At least 75% in equity, with at least 25% each in large cap, mid cap and small cap companies

fact_checks.claim: Multi Cap Fund: Minimum investment in equity & equity related instruments - 75% of total assets ... large cap companies - 25% ... mid cap companies - 25% ... small cap companies - 25% of total assets
Flexi Cap Fund: Minimum Investment in equity & equity related instruments – 65% of total assets

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under SEBI's February 2026 circular on categorisation of mutual fund schemes, what role does AMFI play in the launch of sectoral and thematic funds?

options.text: Mutual funds may launch sectoral/thematic funds only as per the list of sectors/themes published by AMFI, in consultation with SEBI, and updated half-yearly
AMFI sets the maximum expense ratio of each sectoral/thematic scheme every quarter
AMFI must individually approve each sectoral/thematic scheme before its NFO
AMFI computes the portfolio overlap of each scheme and publishes it monthly

solution.concept: AMFI's role in scheme categorisation
solution.explanation: To keep sectoral and thematic funds true to label, the circular requires mutual funds to launch them only from the list of sectors/themes that AMFI publishes and updates half-yearly in consultation with SEBI. Portfolio overlap is disclosed monthly by each AMC on its own website, not by AMFI.
steps: Sector/theme list: AMFI, with SEBI, half-yearly
solution.why_others_wrong: SEBI, not AMFI, approves schemes; expense limits are set by SEBI regulations; AMCs, not AMFI, disclose overlap.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Mutual funds may launch sectoral/thematic funds only as per the list of sectors/themes published by AMFI, in consultation with SEBI, and updated half-yearly

fact_checks.claim: Mutual Funds shall launch sectoral/thematic funds as per the list of sectors/themes as published and updated by AMFI in consultation with SEBI on half yearly basis.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A banking sectoral fund (Scheme A) holds stocks P 20%, Q 15%, R 25%, S 10% and T 30%. The same AMC's flexi cap fund (Scheme B) holds P 10%, Q 25%, R 20%, U 30% and V 15%. Using SEBI's portfolio overlap methodology of February 2026, what is the overlap, and does it meet the limit for sectoral/thematic schemes?

solution.concept: Portfolio overlap between schemes
solution.explanation: Overlap is the sum, over common stocks only, of the lower of the two weights: P min(20,10) = 10, Q min(15,25) = 15, R min(25,20) = 20; S, T, U and V count zero. Total = 45%. A sectoral/thematic scheme may overlap no more than 50% with other equity schemes (except large cap schemes), so 45% is within the limit.
solution.why_others_wrong: 60% adds Scheme A's weights of the common stocks, 55% adds Scheme B's, and 57.5% averages the two; the method takes the minimum weight of each common stock.

fact_checks.claim: For each common scrip, the minimum weightage between the two schemes shall be considered. The overall portfolio overlap between the two schemes shall be the sum of such minimum weightages of all common scrips
no more than 50% of the schemes portfolios would overlap with other equity schemes in sectoral/thematic category and other equity schemes categories except for large cap scheme.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Ravi invested in a Life Cycle Fund launched under SEBI's February 2026 framework and redeems all his 2,000 units 18 months later, when the applicable NAV is ₹15. Using Redemption Price = Applicable NAV × (1 − exit load), how much does he receive?

solution.concept: Exit load and redemption price
solution.explanation: Life Cycle Funds carry a mandatory exit load to instil discipline: 3% on exit within one year, 2% within the first two years and 1% within the first three years. At 18 months the 2% load applies: redemption price = 15 × 0.98 = ₹14.70, and 2,000 × 14.70 = ₹29,400.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹29,100 applies the first-year 3% load; ₹29,700 applies the third-year 1% load; ₹30,000 ignores the exit load.

fact_checks.claim: an exit load of 3% would be chargeable on any exit by an investor within one year of investment; an exit load of 2% within first two years of investment and 1% in the first three years of investment.
Redemption Price = Applicable NAV*(1- Exit Load, if any)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to IRDAI's Annual Report 2024-25, released in December 2025, what was India's overall insurance penetration (life and non-life together) in 2024-25?

options.text: 7.3%, in line with the world average

solution.concept: Insurance penetration (premium as a share of GDP)
solution.explanation: IRDAI's Annual Report 2024-25 put overall insurance penetration at 3.7% in 2024-25, the same as in 2023-24. Life penetration alone slipped to 2.7% from 2.8%. Overall penetration had peaked at 4.2% in 2021-22 and has since declined.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.2% was the 2021-22 peak, not the 2024-25 level; 2.7% (down from 2.8%) is life penetration alone; 7.3% is far above India's level.

fact_checks.claim: The overall insurance penetration (life and non-life) remained flat at 3.7 per cent as in 2023-24. Insurance penetration in India had peaked at 4.2 per cent during the pandemic in 2021-22 but has since declined. ... life insurance penetration which has declined to 2.7 per cent during 2024-25 from 2.8 per cent in the previous year
Overall, insurance penetration stood unchanged at 3.7% in 2024–25, the same level as in 2023–24

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), what is the maximum premium payable by farmers for Kharif and Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops respectively?

solution.concept: PMFBY premium structure
solution.explanation: Farmers pay at most 2% for Kharif and 1.5% for Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops, and at most 5% for commercial and horticultural crops. The rest of the premium is subsidised by the Centre and the States.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.5% and 2% reverses the seasons; 5% applies only to commercial and horticultural crops.

fact_checks.claim: Farmers pay a maximum premium of 2% for Kharif and 1.5% for Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops. For commercial and horticultural crops, the maximum premium is 5%.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Bill, 2025, the category of 'insurance intermediaries' (which already included brokers, insurance consultants and third-party administrators) is broadened to also include:

options.text: Managing general agents and insurance repositories
Banks and NBFCs acting as corporate agents

solution.concept: Insurance intermediaries and IRDAI's oversight
solution.explanation: The Bill, introduced in Lok Sabha on 16 December 2025, broadens insurance intermediaries to include managing general agents and insurance repositories, and extends IRDAI's powers of inspection and investigation to intermediaries.
steps: Added: managing general agents, insurance repositories
solution.why_others_wrong: The other groups are not the additions named in the Bill; reinsurers are insurers, not intermediaries.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Managing general agents and insurance repositories

fact_checks.claim: Under the Act, intermediaries include brokers, insurance consultants, and third-party administrators. The Bill broadens this to also include managing general agents and insurance repositories.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What change does the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Bill, 2025 make for insurance co-operative societies?

options.text: It bars them from health insurance business
It allows them 100% foreign direct investment through the automatic route
It removes the requirement of a minimum paid-up share capital of ₹100 crore for life, general and health insurance business
It raises their minimum paid-up share capital from ₹100 crore to ₹500 crore

solution.concept: Entry norms for insurers
solution.explanation: The Bill amends the definition of an insurance co-operative society to remove the requirement of a minimum paid-up share capital of ₹100 crore for life, general and health insurance businesses, easing entry for co-operatives.
solution.why_others_wrong: The Bill lowers, not raises, the entry bar; 100% FDI relates to Indian insurance companies; nothing bars health insurance.
solution.final_answer: Option C: It removes the requirement of a minimum paid-up share capital of ₹100 crore for life, general and health insurance business

fact_checks.claim: The Bill amends the definition of an insurance co-operative society to remove the requirement of minimum paid-up share capital of Rs 100 crore for life, general, and health insurance businesses.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A farmer in Assam insures her Kharif paddy under PMFBY for a sum insured of ₹80,000. The actuarial premium rate for the crop is 9%. How is the premium shared among the farmer, the Centre and the State?

solution.concept: PMFBY premium subsidy sharing
solution.explanation: Total premium = 9% × 80,000 = ₹7,200. The farmer pays the Kharif cap of 2% = ₹1,600. The balance ₹5,600 is subsidised; for North-Eastern and Himalayan States the Centre and State share it 90:10, so the Centre pays ₹5,040 and Assam ₹560.
solution.why_others_wrong: 50:50 sharing (₹2,800 each) applies to other States; 1.5% is the Rabi cap; 5% is for commercial and horticultural crops.

fact_checks.claim: Farmers pay a maximum premium of 2% for Kharif and 1.5% for Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops. The Central & State Governments subsidizes the remaining premium in 50:50 proportion. For the farmers in North-Eastern & Himalayan States/UTs, the contribution of Central & State Govt. subsidy is in a 90:10 proportion.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: To produce equipment and materials, design full-stack Indian IP and fortify supply chains, the Union Budget 2026-27 proposed to launch:

solution.concept: Manufacturing in strategic and frontier sectors
solution.explanation: Building on ISM 1.0, the Budget proposed ISM 2.0 to produce semiconductor equipment and materials, design full-stack Indian IP and fortify supply chains, with industry-led research and training centres.
steps: Semiconductor equipment, materials, Indian IP → ISM 2.0
solution.why_others_wrong: The other missions were not announced as '2.0' versions for this purpose in the Budget.

fact_checks.claim: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 2.0 to be launched to produce equipment and materials, design full-stack Indian IP, and fortify supply chains

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: To create a more contemporary, user-friendly framework for foreign investments, the Union Budget 2026-27 proposed a comprehensive review of the:

options.text: Foreign Exchange Management (Current Account Transactions) Rules

solution.concept: Foreign investment framework under FEMA
solution.explanation: Equity-type foreign investment into India (FDI and portfolio investment) is governed by the FEM (Non-debt Instruments) Rules. The Budget proposed a comprehensive review of these Rules to create a more contemporary, user-friendly framework for foreign investments consistent with India's evolving economic priorities.
steps: Inbound equity investment → FEM (Non-debt Instruments) Rules
solution.why_others_wrong: The Debt Instruments Regulations cover debt flows, the Overseas Investment Rules cover outward investment and the Current Account Transactions Rules cover current account payments; none was named for review.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules

fact_checks.claim: Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman proposes a comprehensive review of the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules in the Union Budget to create a more contemporary, user-friendly framework for foreign investments consistent with India's evolving economic priorities.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to the Medium-term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement presented with the Union Budget 2026-27, the medium-term aim is a Central Government debt-to-GDP ratio of 50±1% by 2030-31. Which indicator acts as the operational target?

solution.concept: Debt anchor and operational target
solution.explanation: The fiscal anchor is the debt glide path; to reach it, the fiscal deficit is used as the operational target, set at 4.3% of GDP for BE 2026-27.
solution.why_others_wrong: Revenue, primary and effective revenue deficits are reported but are not the operational target.

fact_checks.claim: The medium-term aim to reach a debt to GDP ratio of 50±1 per cent by FY 2030-31, with the fiscal deficit acting as the operational target.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what were the gross and net NPA ratios of banks in September 2025?

solution.concept: Asset quality of banks
solution.explanation: The Survey reported gross NPAs down to 2.2% and net NPAs to 0.5% by September 2025, with bank credit growing 14.5%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3.9%/1.0% are not the September 2025 levels; the third option swaps the two (net NPAs cannot exceed gross); 7.1% and 1.3% are the FY18 and FY26 slippage ratios.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Gross NPAs 2.2% and net NPAs 0.5%

fact_checks.claim: Gross Non-Performing Assets fell to 2.2 percent, while net NPAs declined to 0.5 percent by September 2025. ... Bank credit growth accelerated to 14.5 percent year-on-year.
Banking sector asset quality improved significantly, with Gross Non-performing Assets (NPA) at 2.2% and net NPA at 0.5% in September 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Centre's capital expenditure of ₹12.22 lakh crore in BE 2026-27 includes capital support to States through SASCI. What is SASCI, and what is its outlay?

options.text: State Allocation for Social and Capital Investment; ₹1.4 lakh crore
Scheme for Aid to States for Capital Infrastructure; ₹2.0 lakh crore as revenue grants
Special Assistance as Loan to States for Capital Expenditure; ₹4.93 lakh crore
Special Assistance as Loan to States for Capital Expenditure; ₹2.0 lakh crore

solution.concept: Capital support to States
solution.explanation: SASCI (Special Assistance as Loan to States for Capital Expenditure) has an outlay of ₹2.0 lakh crore in BE 2026-27 and is counted in the Centre's capital expenditure, since it is a loan, not a grant.
steps: SASCI = Special Assistance as Loan to States for Capital Expenditure
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1.4 lakh crore is FC grants; ₹4.93 lakh crore is grants-in-aid for capital assets; SASCI is a loan, not a revenue grant.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Special Assistance as Loan to States for Capital Expenditure; ₹2.0 lakh crore

fact_checks.claim: This includes capital support to States through SASCI (Special Assistance as Loan to States for Capital Expenditure) with an outlay of ₹2.0 lakh crore.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 urged India to move from import substitution and 'strategic resilience' towards which goal?

solution.concept: Theme of the Economic Survey 2025-26
solution.explanation: The Survey's framing is a shift from 'Strategic Resilience' (the ability to withstand shocks) to 'Strategic Indispensability', making India hard to replace in key global supply chains.
steps: Import substitution → strategic resilience → strategic indispensability
solution.why_others_wrong: Autonomy, decoupling and self-sufficiency are not the Survey's named goal.

fact_checks.claim: The Survey calls for a shift from Strategic Resilience to Strategic Indispensability
Eco Survey maps swadeshi path to strategic resilience, indispensability

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's services exports in FY25 reached a record of:

solution.concept: External sector
solution.explanation: Services exports reached a record USD 387.6 billion in FY25 (+13.6%), helping total exports hit a record USD 825.3 billion (+6.1%). Remittances were a record USD 135.4 billion.
solution.why_others_wrong: USD 825.3 bn is total exports; USD 135.4 bn is remittances; USD 701.4 bn is forex reserves.

fact_checks.claim: Total exports touched a record USD 825.3 bn in FY25 (6.1% YoY growth) ... services exports at an all-time high of USD 387.6 bn (13.6% YoY growth) ... record remittances of USD 135.4 bn

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 noted that the Centre's capital expenditure rose from ₹2.63 lakh crore in FY18 to ₹11.21 lakh crore in FY26 (BE). Over these eight years, at roughly what compound annual growth rate (CAGR) did central capex grow?

solution.concept: Growth of public capex; compound annual growth rate
solution.explanation: The multiple is 11.21 ÷ 2.63 ≈ 4.26 (the Survey calls it a rise of 4.2 times). FY18 to FY26 is 8 years, so CAGR = 4.26^(1/8) − 1 ≈ 0.199, i.e. about 20% a year (check: 1.2^8 ≈ 4.3).
solution.shortcut: Test round rates: 1.2^2 = 1.44, 1.2^4 ≈ 2.07, 1.2^8 ≈ 4.3, which matches the 4.26 multiple.
solution.why_others_wrong: 17.5% spreads the growth over 9 years and 23% over 7; 41% is a simple average (326% ÷ 8) that ignores compounding.

fact_checks.claim: central capex rising 4.2 times from Rs 2.63 lakh crore (FY18) to Rs 11.21 lakh crore (FY26 BE)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on the Macro-economic Framework Statement presented with the Union Budget 2026-27:
I. Gross fixed capital formation rose by 7.8% in FY26, and its share has stayed at around 30% of GDP for the past three years.
II. Gross FDI inflows were USD 81.0 billion in FY25.
III. Growth of government final consumption expenditure slowed from 5.2% in FY25 to 2.3% in FY26.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.concept: Macro-economic Framework Statement
solution.explanation: GFCF rose 7.8% in FY26 with its share stable at about 30% of GDP (I true). Gross FDI inflows were USD 81.0 billion in FY25 (II true). Government final consumption expenditure is estimated to rebound to 5.2% growth in FY26 from 2.3% in FY25, so III reverses the years and is false.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every option containing III is wrong; 'I and II only' is the only one with both true statements alone.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) rising by 7.8 per cent in FY26, higher than the previous year. Further, the share of GFCF has remained stable at around 30 per cent of GDP for the past three years.

Government final consumption expenditure is also estimated to strongly rebound with a YoY growth of 5.2 per cent in FY26 as against 2.3 per cent in FY25. Gross Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows were recorded at USD 81.0 billion in FY25

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Match the following FY 2025-26 growth estimates (first advance estimates, as cited in the Budget's Macro-economic Framework Statement):
P. Nominal GDP   Q. Services sector   R. Manufacturing and construction   S. Agriculture
1. 3.1%   2. 7.0%   3. 8.0%   4. 9.1%

solution.concept: Sectoral growth in FY26
solution.explanation: Nominal GDP is estimated to grow 8%, services (the main growth driver) 9.1%, manufacturing and construction 7% and agriculture 3.1% in FY 2025-26.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options swap nominal GDP with services or manufacturing; services, not nominal GDP, grew fastest.
solution.final_answer: Option D: P-3, Q-4, R-2, S-1

fact_checks.claim: India's real GDP is estimated to grow by 7.4 per cent in FY 2025–26, with nominal GDP growth at 8 per cent. The services sector remains the primary growth driver, expanding by 9.1 per cent. Manufacturing and construction have grown by 7 per cent. Agriculture is estimated to grow at 3.1 per cent.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that ₹36.18 lakh crore had been disbursed under Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana across 55.45 crore loan accounts. What is the average loan per account, and in which PMMY category would a loan of that size fall?

solution.concept: Scale of MUDRA lending
solution.explanation: ₹36.18 lakh crore = ₹36.18 × 10¹² and 55.45 crore = 55.45 × 10⁷, so the average is about ₹65,250. Shishu covers loans up to ₹50,000 and Kishor above ₹50,000 up to ₹5 lakh, so the average lies in Kishor.
steps: Above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh → Kishor
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹65,000 exceeds the ₹50,000 Shishu limit; ₹6.5 lakh and ₹6,500 misplace the decimal by a factor of ten.

fact_checks.claim: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana ... has disbursed Rs 36.18 lakh crore across 55.45 crore loan accounts.
Shishu – upto Rs.50,000; Kishore– Above Rs.50,000 and upto Rs.5 lakh; Tarun- Above Rs.5 lakh and upto Rs.10 lakh

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: MUDRA, the refinancing agency behind Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana, was converted on 6 January 2016 into a wholly owned subsidiary of which institution?

options.text: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

solution.concept: Institutional set-up of MUDRA
solution.explanation: MUDRA was launched on 8 April 2015 as a subsidiary of SIDBI; on 6 January 2016 it became a wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI and was renamed MUDRA (SIDBI) Bank. It refinances member lending institutions rather than lending to micro units directly.
steps: 6 January 2016: wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI → MUDRA (SIDBI) Bank
solution.why_others_wrong: NABARD, RBI and SBI do not own MUDRA.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

fact_checks.claim: On 6 January 2016 it became a wholly owned SIDBI subsidiary and was renamed MUDRA (SIDBI) Bank.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to the Department of Financial Services, which of the following is correct about Atal Pension Yojana (APY)?

options.text: The minimum period of contribution is 20 years or more, and a subscriber may exit voluntarily before 60 on deduction of the Government co-contribution and the return on it
The minimum period of contribution is 20 years or more, and voluntary exit before 60 is not permitted in any case
The minimum period of contribution is 15 years, and a subscriber may exit voluntarily before 60 on forfeiting all contributions
The minimum period of contribution is 10 years, and a subscriber who exits voluntarily before 60 gets the full corpus including the Government co-contribution

solution.concept: APY contribution period and voluntary exit
solution.explanation: Pension under APY begins at 60 and the latest joining age is 40, so every subscriber contributes for at least 20 years. Subscribers can also exit voluntarily before 60, subject to conditions, but the Government co-contribution and the return on it are deducted from what they get back.
steps: Pension starts at 60; latest entry at 40 → at least 20 years of contribution
Voluntary exit allowed; Government co-contribution and its return deducted
solution.why_others_wrong: 10 and 15 years understate the minimum period; voluntary exit is allowed; on exit the subscriber does not get the Government co-contribution, nor forfeit his own contributions.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The minimum period of contribution is 20 years or more, and a subscriber may exit voluntarily before 60 on deduction of the Government co-contribution and the return on it

fact_checks.claim: Therefore, minimum period of contribution by any subscriber under APY would be 20 years or more. Subscribers can also voluntarily exit from APY subject to certain conditions, on deduction of Government co-contribution and return/interest thereon.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the PM Vidyalaxmi scheme for students admitted on merit to Quality Higher Educational Institutions, what credit guarantee does the Government of India give to lenders?

solution.concept: Credit guarantee for education loans
solution.explanation: To encourage lending, the Government provides a 75% credit guarantee on PM Vidyalaxmi education loans of up to ₹7.5 lakh. ₹10 lakh is the loan limit for the 3% interest subvention, not for the guarantee.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹10 lakh is the subvention ceiling; 100% and 50% are not the guarantee rates.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 75% for loans up to ₹7.5 lakh

fact_checks.claim: Loans up to ₹ 7.5 lakhs are provided 75% credit guarantee by Government of India, to support banks to expand coverage.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC), which acts as a common trustee for several credit guarantee funds, was set up by:

options.text: RBI, under Section 17 of the RBI Act, 1934, in 1962
The Department of Financial Services, incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 on 28 March 2014
NABARD, under the NABARD Act, 1981, in 2010
SIDBI and the Ministry of MSME, as a trust registered in July 2000

solution.concept: Institutions for credit guarantees
solution.explanation: Following credit guarantee announcements in the 2013-14 Budget, the Department of Financial Services set up NCGTC, incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 on 28 March 2014 with paid-up capital of ₹10 crore, as a common trustee company to manage various credit guarantee trust funds.
steps: Set up by DFS, Ministry of Finance
Incorporated 28 March 2014 under the Companies Act, 1956
solution.why_others_wrong: The SIDBI/MSME trust of July 2000 is CGTMSE; RBI and NABARD did not set up NCGTC.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The Department of Financial Services, incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 on 28 March 2014

fact_checks.claim: incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 on March 28, 2014 with a paid up capital of ₹10 crore; set up by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India to act as a common trustee company to manage and operate various credit guarantee trust funds

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following credit guarantee funds is NOT listed among the funds under NCGTC's trusteeship?

options.text: Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand Up India (CGFSI)
Credit Guarantee Fund for Education Loans (CGFEL)
Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)

solution.concept: Credit guarantee institutions
solution.explanation: NCGTC acts as trustee for funds such as CGFSD (skill development), CGFEL (education loans), CGFF (factoring), CGFMU (micro units), CGFSI (Stand-Up India), ECLGS and CGSS (startups). CGTMSE is a separate trust set up by SIDBI and the Ministry of MSME.
steps: NCGTC funds: CGFSD, CGFEL, CGFF, CGFMU, CGFSI, ECLGS, CGSS …
solution.why_others_wrong: CGFSI, CGFEL and CGFF are all on NCGTC's list of funds.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)

fact_checks.claim: Funds under its trusteeship: Credit Guarantee Fund for Skill Development (CGFSD), Credit Guarantee Fund for Education Loans (CGFEL), Credit Guarantee Fund for Factoring (CGFF), Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU), Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand Up India (CGFSI)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Two students secure merit admission to Quality Higher Educational Institutions and take PM Vidyalaxmi education loans; neither gets any other scholarship or subvention. A borrows ₹7 lakh and her annual family income is ₹9 lakh. B borrows ₹12 lakh and his family income is ₹6 lakh. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A's loan gets the guarantee and 3% subvention; B gets subvention of ₹36,000 a year during the moratorium
A's loan gets neither benefit; B's loan gets the 75% guarantee and subvention of ₹30,000 a year
A's loan gets the 75% guarantee but no subvention; B's loan gets no guarantee but subvention of ₹30,000 a year during the moratorium
A's loan gets the 75% guarantee but no subvention; B gets the guarantee on ₹7.5 lakh and subvention of ₹36,000 a year

solution.concept: PM Vidyalaxmi: guarantee and interest subvention
solution.explanation: The 75% guarantee is for loans up to ₹7.5 lakh, so A (₹7 lakh) is covered and B (₹12 lakh) is not. The 3% subvention is for family income up to ₹8 lakh and on loans up to ₹10 lakh (only the first ₹10 lakh of a bigger loan), during the moratorium: A (₹9 lakh income) gets none; B gets 3% × ₹10 lakh = ₹30,000 a year.
steps: Guarantee: A yes (≤ ₹7.5 lakh), B no
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹36,000 applies 3% to the whole ₹12 lakh; B's loan exceeds the ₹7.5 lakh guarantee limit; A qualifies for the guarantee.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A's loan gets the 75% guarantee but no subvention; B's loan gets no guarantee but subvention of ₹30,000 a year during the moratorium

fact_checks.claim: Loans up to ₹ 7.5 lakhs are provided 75% credit guarantee by Government of India. For students with up to ₹ 8 lakhs annual family income, the scheme provides for 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹ 10 lakh.
If the education loan amount is more than ₹ 10 lakhs, interest subvention is provided for the disbursed total principal amount of the loan up to ₹ 10 lakhs only.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about PM Vidyalaxmi education loans:
I. The interest rate is capped at the lending bank's External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) plus 0.5%.
II. The loan is repayable over up to 15 years, excluding a moratorium of the course period plus one year.
III. There is no cap on the number of students who can receive the 3% interest subvention in a year.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.concept: PM Vidyalaxmi loan terms
solution.explanation: Interest is capped at the bank's EBLR + 0.5% (I) and repayment runs up to 15 years after a moratorium of course period plus one year (II). A maximum of one lakh students a year are eligible for the 3% subvention, so III is false (the no-limit rule is for PM-USP CSIS beneficiaries).
steps: III: capped at 1 lakh students a year → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The interest rates charged on the educational loan under the scheme will be capped at the individual bank's Externally Benchmarked Lending Rate (EBLR) + 0.5%. The repayment period of the education loan is up to 15 years, excluding a moratorium period of the course period plus one year.
In a year, a maximum of one lakh students shall be eligible for 3% interest subvention during the moratorium period. No such limit is for CSIS beneficiaries.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: IBM's System/360 family of the mid-1960s replaced discrete transistors with integrated circuits (ICs), each holding many transistors on one small silicon chip. To which generation of computers do IC-based machines like this belong?

solution.concept: Generations of computers
solution.explanation: First generation: vacuum tubes. Second: transistors. Third: integrated circuits (SSI/MSI chips), which made computers smaller, cheaper and more reliable. Fourth: microprocessors (VLSI). Fifth: AI-oriented, ULSI and parallel processing.
solution.why_others_wrong: First generation used vacuum tubes and second generation discrete transistors. Fifth generation refers to AI-oriented, massively parallel systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: India's Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) builds the PARAM series of machines, which are used for weather forecasting, drug discovery and other research needing enormous calculation speed. What type of computer is a PARAM machine?

solution.concept: Types of computers by capacity
solution.explanation: PARAM is C-DAC's family of supercomputers, starting with PARAM 8000 in the early 1990s; newer systems have been installed under the National Supercomputing Mission.
solution.why_others_wrong: Minicomputers are mid-sized multi-user machines, embedded computers control one device, and personal computers serve one user; none is meant for national-scale scientific computing.

fact_checks.claim: PARAM is a series of supercomputers designed and assembled by C-DAC, Pune; PARAM 8000 was unveiled around 1990-91.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's old data link sends 8-bit codes using EVEN parity, so every correctly received code must contain an even number of 1s. Which received code must have been corrupted on the way?

solution.concept: Parity check
solution.explanation: With even parity, the sender sets the parity bit so that the total number of 1s is even. A received code with an odd number of 1s is therefore certainly wrong. 10110101 has five 1s (odd). The other three codes have four or six 1s.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11000011, 10101010 and 01111110 each have an even number of 1s, so they pass the even-parity check.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A register holds the 8-bit value 00010110. The processor shifts all bits two places to the LEFT, filling the empty places with 0 (no 1-bit is lost). What decimal value does the register now hold?

solution.concept: Binary shift = multiply by a power of 2
solution.explanation: 00010110 = 16 + 4 + 2 = 22. Shifting left by one place doubles a binary number; by two places it multiplies by 4. 01011000 = 64 + 16 + 8 = 88.
solution.shortcut: Left shift by n multiplies by 2^n (while no 1-bit falls off).
solution.why_others_wrong: 44 is a shift by only one place. 176 is a shift by three places. 24 just adds 2.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The bank's website uses the colour code #FF8C00 for its buttons. Such a code gives the red, green and blue intensities as three pairs of hexadecimal digits (RRGGBB). What are the decimal intensities?

solution.concept: Hexadecimal colour codes
solution.explanation: Split into pairs: FF, 8C, 00. FF = 15 x 16 + 15 = 255. 8C = 8 x 16 + 12 = 140. 00 = 0. So red 255, green 140, blue 0 (an orange shade).
solution.why_others_wrong: 128 would be 80 in hex. 15 reads only one F. 12 wrongly takes C as a separate blue value.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A hex dump of a file shows the four bytes 42 41 4E 4B. In ASCII, 'A' is 41 (hex) and the capital letters follow in alphabetical order. What text do these bytes spell?

solution.concept: Hexadecimal and ASCII
solution.explanation: 41 = A, so 42 = B. 4E is 41 + D (13) places on: A + 13 = N. 4B is A + 10 = K. The text is BANK.
solution.why_others_wrong: BAMK reads 4E as M (4D). CANK takes 42 as C (43). BANL reads 4B as L (4C).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In the 1640s a French mathematician built a mechanical calculating machine with toothed wheels to help his father, a tax collector, with additions. Who built this machine, and what is it called?

solution.concept: Early calculating machines
solution.explanation: Blaise Pascal invented the Pascaline in the 1640s for his tax-collector father; it could add (subtraction was done by complements). It is one of the earliest mechanical calculators.
solution.why_others_wrong: Babbage's Difference Engine is from the 1820s. Leibniz's Stepped Reckoner (1670s) could also multiply. Napier's bones (1617) were numbered rods, not a geared machine.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Blaise Pascal - the Pascaline

fact_checks.claim: CHM: In the 1640s Pascal invented for his father, a tax collector, a machine that could add.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In 1804 a French weaver built a loom whose weaving pattern was controlled by a chain of punched cards; Charles Babbage later planned to use punched cards to feed instructions to his Analytical Engine. Who built this loom?

solution.concept: Punched cards in computing history
solution.explanation: Joseph-Marie Jacquard's loom (1804) used punched cards to select which threads were lifted, so the pattern could be changed by changing the cards. Babbage borrowed the idea for the Analytical Engine, and Hollerith later used punched cards for census data.
solution.why_others_wrong: Hollerith used punched cards for the 1890 US census, not for weaving. Pascal built an adding machine. Zuse built early electromechanical computers in the 1930s-40s.

fact_checks.claim: CHM: Jacquard developed his card control for power looms in 1804; Babbage designed the Analytical Engine with a control mechanism using loops of punched cards.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In the 1970s, a regional office ran its accounts on a mid-sized computer that was much cheaper and smaller than a mainframe but still served about 30 terminals at the same time, such as a DEC PDP or VAX machine. In the size-based classification, what is such a computer called?

solution.concept: Types of computers by size
solution.explanation: Minicomputers sit between mainframes and microcomputers: multi-user machines for a department or medium-sized organisation. DEC's PDP and VAX lines are classic examples. Today mid-range servers fill this role.
steps: Multi-user, smaller than a mainframe, bigger than a PC = minicomputer
solution.why_others_wrong: A microcomputer is a single-user PC. A supercomputer is for very heavy scientific work. A thin client is a terminal that depends on a server.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A program stores a balance adjustment as a 16-bit signed integer in two's complement form. Its memory shows the hexadecimal value FF9C. What decimal value does it represent?

solution.concept: 16-bit two's complement
solution.explanation: The leading hex digit F means the sign bit is 1, so the number is negative. Its value is (unsigned value) - 2^16 = 65,436 - 65,536 = -100. Check: +100 = 0064 hex; invert -> FF9B; add 1 -> FF9C.
solution.why_others_wrong: 65,436 reads the bits as unsigned. -99 forgets to add 1 after inverting (one's complement). +100 ignores the sign bit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's app stores text in UTF-8. English letters such as 'A' (U+0041) take 1 byte each. How many bytes does UTF-8 use for the Indian rupee sign (U+20B9)?

solution.concept: UTF-8 variable-length encoding
solution.explanation: UTF-8 uses 1 byte for U+0000-U+007F, 2 bytes for U+0080-U+07FF, 3 bytes for U+0800-U+FFFF and 4 bytes above that. U+20B9 lies in U+0800-U+FFFF, so it takes 3 bytes (E2 82 B9).
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 byte is only for ASCII characters. 2 bytes cover up to U+07FF (e.g. many Latin, Greek and Arabic letters). 4 bytes are for code points above U+FFFF, such as emoji.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a 1936 paper, 'On Computable Numbers', a British mathematician described an abstract machine that reads and writes symbols on an endless tape, one square at a time, following a table of rules. The idea became the theoretical model of a general-purpose computer. Who wrote it?

solution.concept: Theoretical foundations of computing
solution.explanation: Alan Turing's 1936 paper defined what is now called the Turing machine, and showed that one universal machine could imitate any other, the basic idea of a stored-program computer.
steps: 1936 + 'On Computable Numbers' + tape machine = Alan Turing
solution.why_others_wrong: Von Neumann described the stored-program architecture in 1945. Shannon founded information theory (1948). Babbage designed mechanical engines in the 1800s.

fact_checks.claim: Turing's paper 'On Computable Numbers' (1936) described an abstract machine with a tape of symbols read and written by a head following rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A teller PC's specification reads: 'Processor: 6 cores, 3.0 GHz'. What does '3.0 GHz' tell you?

options.text: The processor's clock ticks about 3 billion times per second
The processor can store 3 GB of data
The processor can run 3 programs at once

solution.concept: Clock speed
solution.explanation: GHz (gigahertz) measures the processor's clock frequency. 3.0 GHz = 3 x 10^9 clock cycles per second; each cycle is a step in which the processor can do work.
solution.why_others_wrong: Storage and cache are measured in bytes (MB, GB), not hertz. The number of programs handled at once depends on cores and threads, not on GHz.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The processor's clock ticks about 3 billion times per second

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: While fitting a new heat sink on a processor, a technician first spreads a thin layer of grey paste on top of the processor. What is this paste for?

options.text: It insulates the processor from electric current
It glues the processor permanently into its socket
It fills tiny air gaps so that heat passes better from the processor to the heat sink
It stores the processor's settings when the PC is off

solution.concept: Thermal interface material
